text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Norwegian shipbuilding, engineering and construction group Kvaerner ASA has not suffered any damage from the theft of computer-stored information earlier this year from the Oslo headquarters, Kvaerner's Tore Soerensen said. The police will close the investigation of the case in a couples of weeks.
- Hermod Skanland, former head of Norway's central bank, says the national budget presented on Friday should have been tigther if the government wants to reduce the pressure on the Norwegian economy.

- The Justice Ministry may demand compensation after some rescue operations. Ministry official Ole Hafnor says the department may demand compensation for a part of the operation when rescued people have shown gross negligence.

- Norway is the most Swedish country besides Sweden. No other country is so eager to buy Swedish cars, listen to Swedish music or travel to Sweden. More than 15 percent of Norway's total import is from Sweden.
- The market for ecologically-produced food is growing, but producers are having problems keeping up with demand.
